prompt: What does the passage name as the first manifestation of divine wisdom?

options.text: Creativity
Exploits
Authority
Joy

explanation: 'The first manifestation of divine wisdom was in creativity', proved from Genesis 1:1-3. The others follow in order: exploits, authority, joy, wealth, pleasantness and peace, dominion, and answers.

why.a: Correct. Creativity is explicitly called the first, and creation itself is the proof.
why.b: Wrong. Exploits comes second in the chapter's order.
why.c: Wrong. Authority comes third.
why.d: Wrong. Joy comes fourth.

prompt: How does the passage define creativity?

options.text: The ability to tread realms no one has treaded before and still get results, and to operate as a pace-setter in your calling
The ability to improve on what others have already made
The ability to see beauty where others see nothing
The ability to solve problems quickly under pressure

explanation: Two halves: untrodden realms with results, and pace-setting in your calling and endeavour. Divine wisdom gives the ability to bring into being things that hitherto did not exist.

why.a: Correct. Both halves of the definition are given in the text.
why.b: Wrong. Improvement is too weak; the claim is about realms no one has trodden.
why.c: Wrong. Beauty is not the category used.
why.d: Wrong. Speed under pressure is closer to what wisdom's peace removes than to creativity.

prompt: Which scripture does the passage call the philosophy of divine wisdom?

options.text: "Behold I do a new thing", Isaiah 43:19
"By me kings reign and princes decree justice", Proverbs 8:15
"The LORD by wisdom hath founded the earth", Proverbs 3:19
"Happy is the man that findeth wisdom", Proverbs 3:13

explanation: Isaiah 43:19 is called the philosophy of divine wisdom because divine wisdom constantly initiates new things and is not afraid to take new steps. The same verse appears again in Chapter 9 against the trap of past failures.

why.a: Correct. Behold I do a new thing is named as its philosophy.
why.b: Wrong. Proverbs 8:15 is quoted under AUTHORITY, a later product in the same chapter.
why.c: Wrong. Proverbs 3:19 is quoted for creativity, but as evidence rather than as the philosophy.
why.d: Wrong. Proverbs 3:13 is quoted under JOY.

prompt: What does the author say about a person who leaves their job the way it was given to them?

options.text: That they are not better than a machine, since a machine could have been put on the job because it cannot think
That they will be passed over for promotion
That they have not yet found their true calling
That they are wasting the years God has given them

explanation: 'If you leave your job the way it was given to you, you're not better than a machine!' The reason follows: a machine cannot think, so if you add no thought you add nothing a machine could not.

why.a: Correct. The machine comparison is the point, and it turns on the machine's inability to think.
why.b: Wrong. The passage says the opposite outcome for the creative: you will always win the commendation of your boss.
why.c: Wrong. Calling is not the issue; approach to the work is.
why.d: Wrong. Wasted years are not the charge made here.

prompt: Which figure is given as an example of creating what you need rather than waiting for it?

options.text: Jacob, in Genesis 30, who created what he needed to beat Laban to his tricks
Joseph, who stored grain against the famine
Isaac, who sowed in the land and reaped a hundredfold
Daniel, who interpreted what no one else could

explanation: Jacob, offered against the assumption that everything needed has already been created. The context is that we are heirs of God and joint-heirs with Christ, so we join Him in the continuous process of creation.

why.a: Correct. Jacob and Laban, cited to Genesis 30.
why.b: Wrong. Joseph's preservation of food appears in Chapter 6 under inspiration.
why.c: Wrong. Isaac's sowing appears in Chapter 7 under separation, and in Chapter 6 as harvest without rain.
why.d: Wrong. Daniel is the wisdom and dominion figure, not the creativity one.

prompt: What does the passage say mighty works are products of?

options.text: A mighty source, divine wisdom
Long preparation and hard labour
The faith of those who receive them
The corporate prayer of the church

explanation: 'Mighty works are products of a mighty source divine wisdom.' The proof texts are Matthew 13:54 and Mark 6:2, where the astonishment joins wisdom and mighty works in one question.

why.a: Correct. A mighty source, named as divine wisdom.
why.b: Wrong. The book's whole point is that one striking insight outweighs a lifetime of struggles.
why.c: Wrong. The faith of recipients is never discussed in this book.
why.d: Wrong. Corporate prayer is not raised anywhere.

prompt: What phrase does the passage use for how Jesus dealt with the spirits He cast out?

options.text: He gave them wisdom knockouts, ordering them out rather than talking or praying them out
He commanded them by the authority of the written word
He rebuked them with a loud voice
He bound them before casting them out

explanation: Wisdom knockouts is the author's own phrase. The distinction that follows is precise: not talking them out, not praying them out, but ORDERING them out.

why.a: Correct. Wisdom knockouts, with the three-way distinction attached.
why.b: Wrong. The written word is not what the passage credits here.
why.c: Wrong. Volume is not mentioned; authority is.
why.d: Wrong. Binding is standard deliverance vocabulary that this book does not use.

prompt: What chain does the passage draw from joy?

options.text: When there is joy there is health, and when there is health long life is guaranteed
When there is joy there is strength, and when there is strength there is victory
When there is joy there is peace, and when there is peace there is prosperity
When there is joy there is faith, and when there is faith there are miracles

explanation: Joy, then health, then long life. It follows the claim that divine wisdom communicates joy unspeakable, full of glory, and that this excitement is what opens you up to mental excellence.

why.a: Correct. The three links are joy, health, long life.
why.b: Wrong. The joy of the Lord being strength is a genuine verse from elsewhere that the book does not use here.
why.c: Wrong. Peace is a separate product with its own section.
why.d: Wrong. Faith and miracles are not part of this chain.

topic: wealth is a product of wits
prompt: How does the passage describe the origin of wealth?

options.text: Wealth is a product of wits, a product of man's Intelligence Quotient
Wealth is a product of consistent giving
Wealth is a product of favour with those in authority
Wealth is a product of long and patient labour

explanation: 'Wealth is a product of wits... a product of man's Intelligence Quotient (IQ).' Somebody is quoted saying wealth is the product of man's capacity to think.

why.a: Correct. Wits and IQ are both named, keeping wealth inside this book's mental scheme.
why.b: Wrong. Giving is part of the prosperity covenant in Chapter 4, but wisdom there insists giving alone is not enough.
why.c: Wrong. Favour is a product of good understanding in Proverbs 13:15, not the origin of wealth.
why.d: Wrong. Labour is required to create channels, but the book credits wealth to thinking.

prompt: What point does the poultry analogy make?

options.text: That as the chickens and their wealth belong to the farm's owner, so you and everything you own are God's
That God feeds those who cannot feed themselves
That small beginnings can become great enterprises
That every creature has a purpose assigned to it

explanation: It follows Psalm 24:1, that the earth is the Lord's and the fulness thereof. The conclusion drawn is that you are created for His pleasure, because you are in His farm.

why.a: Correct. The ownership parallel is the whole analogy, running from chickens to you.
why.b: Wrong. Provision is not the point; ownership is.
why.c: Wrong. Growth from small beginnings is not what the chickens illustrate.
why.d: Wrong. Purpose is discussed elsewhere, but the analogy here is about who owns what.

prompt: What does the passage say mounting pressure indicates?

options.text: That divine wisdom is receding, because wisdom does not walk along the same path as pressures
That God is testing your patience
That a breakthrough is close at hand
That you have taken on more than you were called to

explanation: 'When you see pressure mounting, there is something reducing somewhere.' The thing reducing is divine wisdom, since her ways are ways of pleasantness and all her paths are peace.

why.a: Correct. Pressure rising means wisdom receding, because the two do not share a path.
why.b: Wrong. Testing is not a category this book uses for pressure; pressure is said to be of the devil.
why.c: Wrong. This is a common encouragement the book does not offer.
why.d: Wrong. Overreach is never diagnosed; the book urges more ambition, not less.

prompt: What does the passage say about the source and purpose of pressure?

options.text: Pressure is of the devil, who gathers it around you to steal your blessings and rob you of your substance
Pressure is neutral and becomes good or bad by how you respond
Pressure is God's way of driving you to prayer
Pressure is the natural result of ambition

explanation: Both source and motive are named. It closes with a command that every Satan-gathered pressure disappear.

why.a: Correct. Of the devil, and gathered in order to steal and rob.
why.b: Wrong. The book assigns it a source rather than treating it as neutral.
why.c: Wrong. This would make pressure God's instrument, which contradicts the passage.
why.d: Wrong. Ambition is encouraged throughout, and never blamed for pressure.

prompt: Over whom does the passage say divine wisdom made Daniel master?

options.text: The Chaldeans, astrologers, magicians, sorcerers, witches and wizards
The princes and governors of the provinces
The armies of Babylon
The scribes and lawyers of his day

explanation: The list under DOMINION is the longest version in the book. Elsewhere it appears shorter, as magicians, Chaldeans, astrologers and sorcerers.

why.a: Correct. This six-item list is the one given under dominion, and witches and wizards are what extend it.
why.b: Wrong. Civil administration is not what the book emphasises about Daniel.
why.c: Wrong. Armies never appear in this book.
why.d: Wrong. Scribes and lawyers belong to the Jesus material, where doctors of law could not match His wits.

prompt: Which scripture is cited for the doctors being astounded at Jesus' understanding and answers?

options.text: Luke 2:47
Luke 11:13
Luke 14:28
Luke 24:49

explanation: Luke 2:47, under the product ANSWERS. The point made is that no matter the question, divine wisdom has an answer, since there is no one God could refer a question to.

why.a: Correct. Luke 2:47 is the astonished doctors verse.
why.b: Wrong. Luke 11:13 is the Father giving the Holy Spirit to them that ask, in Chapter 3.
why.c: Wrong. Luke 14:28 is the tower builder counting the cost, in Chapter 2.
why.d: Wrong. Luke 24:49 is tarrying until endued with power, in Chapter 3.

prompt: In the illustration of the rich man who goes begging, what two amounts are named?

options.text: He wants to do something costing 16 million naira and has 10 million naira in hand
He wants to do something costing 20 million naira and has 15 million naira in hand
He wants to do something costing 16 million naira and has 6 million naira in hand
He wants to do something costing 10 million naira and has 6 million naira in hand

explanation: Sixteen million wanted, ten million in hand. Told to do something with what he has, he refuses. The author calls him a foolish man.

why.a: Correct. Sixteen million and ten million are the two figures.
why.b: Wrong. Neither number appears in the book.
why.c: Wrong. The target figure is right but the amount in hand is wrong.
why.d: Wrong. Both figures are misremembered here.

prompt: What does the passage say about people who have died of the plague of debt?

options.text: It does not show in the autopsy; what the doctors see is high blood pressure, but the truth is debt-pressure
They died because they were ashamed to ask for help
They died young, before their appointed time
They died leaving their families in bondage

explanation: The pun is the point: high blood pressure on the certificate, debt-pressure in fact. It follows the claim that most of the troubles of man are all self-caused.

why.a: Correct. The autopsy detail and the debt-pressure pun are both in the text.
why.b: Wrong. Shame is not discussed; the rich man in the same passage begs freely.
why.c: Wrong. No claim about dying young is made.
why.d: Wrong. Consequences to families are not raised.

prompt: What does the passage say will happen if borrowing becomes your habit?

options.text: Lying would have dominion over you
You would lose the respect of those you borrow from
You would never be trusted with wealth
You would pass the habit to your children

explanation: 'If borrowing becomes your habit, then lying would have dominion over you.' The author records deciding many years ago that no condition under heaven would bring him to the point of needing to borrow.

why.a: Correct. Lying having dominion is the specific consequence named.
why.b: Wrong. Reputation with lenders is not the concern.
why.c: Wrong. Trust with wealth is not mentioned in this connection.
why.d: Wrong. Inheritance of habits is not raised here.

prompt: Which list does the passage give as the virtues expressed in divine wisdom?

options.text: Long life, riches, pleasantness, happiness, creativity, exploits, joy and dominion
Love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness and goodness
Wisdom, counsel, knowledge and understanding
Insight, foresight, dominion and unequaled creativity

explanation: Said to be some of the products of divine wisdom listed in Proverbs chapter 3, which is why length of days, riches and honour keep recurring in this chapter.

why.a: Correct. This is the summary list at the end of the chapter's products.
why.b: Wrong. That is the fruit of the Spirit from Galatians, which this book never quotes.
why.c: Wrong. That is what the HOLY GHOST is called in Chapter 3, the spirit of wisdom, counsel, knowledge and understanding.
why.d: Wrong, and it is a real list from this book. It is what the treasure of wisdom gives you in Chapter 10, not this summary.

prompt: According to Proverbs 15:13-16 as cited, what is a man of wisdom?

options.text: A happy, healthy and rich man, who will also naturally enjoy honour
A humble, teachable and patient man
A man who is feared by his enemies
A man whose counsel is sought by kings

explanation: Three adjectives plus honour. It closes the WEALTH section, following Proverbs 3:16 on length of days in her right hand and riches and honour in her left.

why.a: Correct. Happy, healthy and rich, with honour following naturally.
why.b: Wrong. Meekness is a requirement for wisdom in Chapter 4, not a description of the wise man here.
why.c: Wrong. Fear by enemies is not claimed; dominion over the forces of wickedness is a different claim.
why.d: Wrong. Kings seeking counsel describes Ahitophel and Daniel, not this verse.

topic: wealth is a product of wits
prompt: Fill the blank: "Wealth is a product of {{1}}."
explanation: Wits. The alliteration with wealth is what makes it stick, and the sentence is expanded immediately as a product of man's Intelligence Quotient.

prompt: According to the passage, mounting pressure is a sign that divine wisdom is increasing in your life.

options.text: True
False

explanation: False, and exactly backwards. Mounting pressure indicates that divine wisdom is RECEDING, because divine wisdom does not walk along the same path as pressures.

why.true: Wrong. It inverts the sentence. Wisdom's ways are pleasantness and all her paths are peace.
why.false: Correct. Pressure rising means something is reducing, and what is reducing is divine wisdom.

prompt: What connection does the passage draw between God's wisdom and God's wealth?

options.text: The wisest Being in the universe is also the wealthiest, and the Bible calls Him the only wise God
God's wealth is held in trust for those who seek wisdom
God's wisdom is shown by how little He needs
God gives wealth only to those who first prove wise

explanation: The argument is by correlation: the wisest is also the wealthiest, and Solomon repeats the pattern in miniature, being the wisest man of his time and also the wealthiest.

why.a: Correct. Both claims are made, and the only wise God is the title cited.
why.b: Wrong. Trusteeship is not the idea; ownership is, per Psalm 24:1.
why.c: Wrong. This inverts the argument entirely.
why.d: Wrong. No such sequence is set out; the correlation is what carries the point.

prompt: What does the passage say about a person with no background in engineering, technology or computers?

options.text: When the creative abilities of God begin to find expression in them, it shows wherever they go
They should seek training in a technical field
They will be limited to the work of their hands
They should partner with those who have such skills

explanation: Creativity here is not a technical aptitude but a way of approaching whatever you already do: you become original in your approach and productively creative, so you cannot be despised because the results speak.

why.a: Correct. The point is that creativity is not confined to technical fields and shows wherever you go.
why.b: Wrong. Retraining is never advised; a different approach to your present task is.
why.c: Wrong. This contradicts the promise being made.
why.d: Wrong. Partnership is not proposed.
